analysis.investment_thesis: Afcons is a reputable Shapoorji Pallonji Group infrastructure contractor with genuine project execution capabilities across marine, metro, and tunnel works — but revenue growth of just 4.8% CAGR over 5 years is deeply underwhelming for a company priced at 24x P/E, and FY25 revenue actually declined to INR 12,548 Cr from INR 13,268 Cr while OCF turned sharply negative.
key_strengths: ROCE of 19.6% is respectable for a construction company; indicates underlying project returns are reasonable
Diversified project mix (marine, metro, highways, tunnels, oil & gas) with international exposure reduces single-sector risk
Shapoorji Pallonji parentage (promoter 50.17%) provides brand, project access, and large balance sheet support
key_risks: Revenue growth of 4.8% CAGR over 5 years is anaemic — in India's infrastructure supercycle, this is a miss; FY25 revenue declined YoY
Finance costs of INR 629 Cr nearly equals net profit of INR 487 Cr in FY25 — the business is earning for its lenders, not its shareholders
D/E of 0.66 is above my preferred ceiling of 0.6, and borrowings rose sharply to INR 3,565 Cr in FY25 from INR 2,062 Cr in FY23
red_flags: OCF turned negative (-INR 132 Cr) in FY25 for the first time in the data series — working capital stress in construction is a classic early warning sign
FCF swung to -INR 470 Cr in FY25 from +INR 25 Cr in FY24; heavy capex (INR 344 Cr) combined with deteriorating operating cash is a serious concern
Promoter holding at exactly 50.17% — barely over the threshold; limited buffer against further dilution given ongoing capital needs
analysis.detailed_analysis:
India's government capex boom should have been rocket fuel for Afcons, but a 5-year revenue CAGR of just 4.8% and an actual revenue decline in FY25 tells me execution or order book quality has been disappointing. Construction companies in India's current environment — with metro projects, port expansion, and road programs — should be growing at 12–18% annually. Afcons is clearly not capturing its fair share, possibly due to SP Group's financial constraints affecting bidding capacity or project selectivity.

The financials are structurally challenging: finance costs of INR 629 Cr consuming virtually all of the INR 487 Cr net profit means equity shareholders are earning almost nothing after paying lenders. This isn't the kind of business I want to own at 24x P/E. Yes, the government infra push is real and multi-year, but there are better-positioned plays with stronger balance sheets and cleaner FCF generation. I'd wait for either a significant price correction or evidence of accelerating order book execution before considering a position.
